headlines.title: Micron drops 5% as tech stocks rattled by China chip breakthrough claims
headlines.summary: Technology stocks tumbled Tuesday as a sell-off in U.S. semiconductor shares spilled into Asian and European markets.
headlines.article_text: Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, ASML shares: tech stocks fall Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Technology stocks tumbled Tuesday as a sell-off in U.S. semiconductor shares spilled into Asian and European markets. China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, reported progress on a new chip structure, intensifying chip competition. Intel and Broadcom CEOs have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the artificial intelligence boom. In this article 9984.T-JP ASML STM IFX-DE SKHY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Technology stocks fell Tuesday, extending a sell-off sparked by worries over artificial intelligence financing and intensifying competition. Memory chip giant Micron was down around 5% in U.S. premarket trading. Other memory-related stocks such as SanDisk , Seagate and Western Digital were all sharply lower. SanDisk fell 5% while Seagate and Western Digital both dropped 7%. The slide, which follows declines on Wall Street on Monday, comes as investors assessed intensifying competition from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT . Micron shares year-to-date. Over the weekend , CXMT announced significant progress in developing a new chip architecture, designed to increase memory density by packing more data into a smaller space. CXMT is China's leading rival to the likes of Micron and South Korean heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. Analysts broadly see CXMT as trailing the U.S. and South Korean memory leaders, which means any advancement from the Chinese firm could add more competition to the market leaders. "Investors are jittery and looking for excuses to take profit on AI-related stocks that have outperformed this year, especially memory stocks," said UBP's senior equity advisor Vey-Sern Ling. "In reality, while the Chinese memory makers can potentially become a threat to global demand-supply balance over time, in the short run they continue to face technology hurdles, especially for more advanced memory like HBM," Ling told CNBC via email. CXMT shares closed 2.8% lower in Shanghai. Global tech stocks slump Adding fuel to the sell-off was a post by Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk, who said China has the ability to scale production once it figures out how to manufacture something. "When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined," Musk said on Monday. European chip stocks also sank in early morning trade, with semiconductor equipment maker ASML down 3.3%, and STMicroelectronics and German chip maker Infineon both down 5%. Dutch firms BE Semiconductor and ASM International were both around 4% lower at the open. Shares of South Korean chip giant SK Hynix, a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications, plunged more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics shed 7.4% — both hitting their lowest levels since August. SK Hynix's U.S.-listed stock was down around 5% in premarket trading. watch now VIDEO 4:30 04:30 Tech shakedown spreads as U.S. heavyweights face fresh selling Squawk Box Europe In Japan, shares of tech-focused investment giant SoftBank Group sank 8.5%. The group, which has significant exposure to the global AI industry through its huge investment in OpenAI, led a broader retreat in Japanese semiconductor and electronics shares. Tokyo Electron , a major supplier of chipmaking equipment, dropped 7.2%, while Advantest , which makes semiconductor testing equipment, declined 2.9%. Other Japanese technology stocks also came under pressure. Lasertec fell over 5%, Disco lost 4.7% and Renesas Electronics shed 5.9%. The declines followed a weak session for technology stocks on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.44% on Monday. U.S. memory chipmaker Micron Technology slid 3.9% as 'Vulnerable' AI sentiment? Phillip Wool, chief market strategist at Rayliant Global Advisors, said CXMT's breakthrough marked a significant milestone for Chinese chipmakers , demonstrating their ability to overcome technology restrictions and potentially challenge established players sooner than expected. But he cautioned that the market reaction appeared disproportionate to the immediate competitive threat, given that CXMT has yet to demonstrate large-scale production and continues to lag Samsung and SK Hynix in market share. "More importantly, we're not even talking about HBM here, and the Korean chipmakers are still unquestionably dominating that space, with very little threat at all from the likes of CXMT or anyone else for the foreseeable future," Wool said. He said the sharp sell-off reflected broader anxiety over the AI trade rather than a fundamental shift in the competitive landscape. "I read that more as a sign of how vulnerable AI sentiment is at this moment," Wool said, warning that volatility could persist as investors reassess chip demand and how long semiconductor manufacturers can sustain their pricing power. The chief executives of Intel and Broadcom have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the AI boom, even as demand for computing infrastructure continues to outstrip supply. Investors are also looking ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and U.S. inflation data, which could provide fresh clues on the outlook for interest rates that often have an inverse correlation with growth stocks. headlines.article_text: Bank earnings October 2026: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Four of the largest U.S. banks reported third-quarter results on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase , Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs and Citigroup . Bank of America and Morgan Stanley will post earnings on Wednesday. The quarter was dominated by headlines around artificial intelligence, IPO uncertainty, high fuel prices and rising borrowing costs. The banks that reported Tuesday put up mixed results. JPMorgan, the biggest U.S. bank by assets and the largest in the world by market capitalization, posted a rare miss. Goldman Sachs, meanwhile, blew past revenue estimates, led by strong equities trading. Earnings calls with company executives, starting with JPMorgan, are underway. Here's what you need to know: JPM posts a rare earnings miss WFC is out with mixed results GS reports a massive revenue beat Citi's earnings report caps off the morning JPMorgan's CFO says deals are being 'delayed' Dimon says AI will 'benefit mankind enormously' 23 Min Ago Goldman shares rise, leading bank stocks Goldman Sachs shares are leading the bank cohort ahead of the market open on Tuesday. Goldman stock is now almost 4% higher, while JPMorgan stock is up about 1%. Citigroup shares are largely unchanged, and Wells Fargo shares are down almost 3%. — Sara Salinas 37 Min Ago Dimon says another percentage point jump in interest rates would magnify economic pain Jamie Dimon, chief executive officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., during the Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, July 15, 2026. Tom Brenner | Bloomberg | Getty Images Financial pain across the U.S. economy would intensify if interest rates rise another percentage point from current levels, JPMorgan's Dimon said. Rates have climbed for much of this year amid persistent inflation concerns, rising fuel costs, heavy demand for capital to finance the AI buildout and worries about mounting government debt. The 10-year Treasury yield — a key benchmark that influences borrowing costs across the economy — reached about 5.3% by the end of September, up from about 4% six months earlier. “Going from [5%] to 6% would be more painful than going from four to five,” Dimon told CNBC in a question-and-answer session with reporters. Asked why another leg higher would magnify the pain for borrowers, Dimon said it was “because everyone's got to pay more for money, and they'll have to roll over at higher rates, and credit spreads might go up with that a little bit.” Dimon repeatedly stressed that he wasn't predicting rates would reach 6%: “I'm not predicting it. I'm simply saying that people need to be prepared for it." — Hugh Son 54 Min Ago Citi's fixed income markets revenue surpasses expectations Citi reported fixed income markets revenue of $4.4 billion, up 4% from last year. The bank said that growth was driven primarily by advances in spread products and other fixed income. Analysts had been expecting the bank to report fixed income markets revenues of just $4.31 billion, according to StreetAccount. — Laya Neelakandan 57 Min Ago Here's how all four banks fared against Wall Street expectations — Marshall Ritzel 1 Hour Ago Dimon says AI will 'benefit mankind enormously' Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan Chase, at the Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit at the US Army War College in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, on July 15, 2026. Saul Loeb | Afp | Getty Images JPMorgan CEO Dimon said he understands that people are concerned about artificial intelligence, including where data centers are built and how that will affect jobs in the future. But he also added that he thinks AI will "benefit mankind enormously." "I think there are short-run vulnerabilities which we've spoken about extensively," he said. "It's kind of a little bit of a massive buildup, and the value may be high enough to pay higher interest costs." — Leslie Picker 1 Hour Ago Citi raises full-year net interest income guidance Citi raised its full-year net interest income guidance, excluding markets, to be up in the mid-to-high 6% range. That's compared with previous guidance of up between 5% and 6%. The bank said growth is primarily driven by continued fee momentum in services, banking and wealth. — Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago JPMorgan CFO says deals pipeline, consumer remain strong JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said on a media call that the deals pipeline remains robust, and he thinks deals are being "delayed rather than canceled." "There are a lot of deals that need to get done that want to get done," he said. "You know, maybe in moments of a little bit of market turmoil, you see, especially in the capital market space, the gap between buyers and sellers can widen temporarily before we find a new level. So we'll see how it goes. But overall, the conditions remain very supportive." Barnum also said when excluding higher spending on gas prices, the underlying consumer spending trends remain resilient. — Ritika Shah and Leslie Picker 1 Hour Ago Citi shares drop slightly Shares of Citigroup fell slightly in premarket trading Tuesday after the bank reported its third-quarter earnings results, despite beating Wall Street expectations on the top and bottom lines. – Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago Citi sees momentum across services Chief executive officer of Citigroup Jane Fraser visits FOX Business Network's "Mornings With Maria" at Fox Business Network Studios on May 29, 2025 in New York City. John Lamparski | Getty Images Citi said it saw a "standout quarter" in services, up 15%. The company also reported a 6% increase in its banking division. In its U.S. consumer cards, the bank said it had "solid momentum" in general purpose cards, which it said contributed to loan growth and a return over 21%. – Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago Goldman Sachs posts record advisory revenue, but the pipeline shrank Goldman's advisory revenue hit $1.65 billion in the third quarter, up 18% from a year earlier, as the firm closed more deals, a figure that the company says is its highest ever. But the bank said its investment banking fee backlog declined from the second quarter, raising questions about the pace of dealmaking in coming quarters. Has Wall Street dealmaking reached a peak, or a temporary plateau? Expenses for the bank also climbed, with operating costs rising 20% from a year earlier to $11.31 billion. They appear mostly to be the "good" expenses that come from higher levels of activity: Transaction-based expenses jumped 54% to $3.02 billion, while compensation and benefits increased 9% to $5.12 billion. Goldman Sachs stock popped 3.6% in premarket trading. — Hugh Son 1 Hour Ago Citigroup reports best third-quarter revenue in a decade Citigroup on Tuesday morning reported its best third-quarter revenue in a decade, which CEO Jane Fraser attributed to "continued discipline and consistent execution of our strategy." headlines.summary: Pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% in the quarter ⁠to $16.76 billion, but medical technology division sales rose just 2.5% to $8.6 billion.
headlines.article_text: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article JNJ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 8:52 08:52 Johnson & Johnson CFO Joseph Wolk on the company’s Q3 results Squawk Box Johnson & Johnson reported a slightly higher-than-expected profit on Tuesday, driven by strong sales of its immune disease treatment, Tremfya, and said it plans to spin off its hips-and-knees business next year. The company said late last year it intended to spin off its orthopedics unit, DePuy Synthes, into a standalone company, marking its second major spinoff as it sharpens its focus on higher-growth healthcare segments. Chief Financial Officer Joe Wolk said in an interview with CNBC that the company is targeting mid-2027 for the spinoff. "We're not cash strapped. We don't have to pursue a deal that maybe is not optimal," Wolk told CNBC. "We can sit this out for a little bit, separate the business sometime next year." Global alternative asset manager Apollo Global Management is in talks to acquire the orthopedics unit in a ​deal that could value it at close to $20 billion, Bloomberg News reported in September. The company's shares fell 2% before the bell. Middle East conflict weighs on MedTech J&J CFO Wolk told Reuters in an interview that the Middle East conflict, austerity measures in Europe, and pricing in China continued to weigh on international results, "but maybe in a little bit more pronounced way." He said the Middle East conflict, which has driven up fuel costs at home and abroad, has not yet affected the company's costs but has hurt sales in the region. "These are countries that still value and actually want premium healthcare systems, think Kuwait, UAE, Saudi Arabia. They pride themselves on having solid healthcare, very good healthcare," Wolk said. "But their budgets now are being resourced and allocated towards defense." Medical technology division sales rose only 2.5% to $8.6 billion overall, but missed estimates of $8.71 billion, according to LSEG data. Outside the U.S., the division's sales were essentially flat. In MedTech, cardio and surgery drove the miss, J.P. Morgan analyst Chris Schott said. The company raised its full-year reported sales forecast to about $101.2 billion at the midpoint, up from $101.1 billion previously. It increased its adjusted earnings forecast range with a new midpoint of $11.10 per share, up from $11.04. Sales at its Abiomed heart pump business also remained slow after a UK study earlier this year raised questions about using Impella pumps during certain high-risk ​coronary procedures. Quarterly pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% to $16.76 billion. Tremfya sales rose 68% to $2.4 billion, beating analysts' estimates of about $2.19 billion, while Stelara sales, which face generic competition, fell 54% to $716 million, still well above Wall Street expectations of $591 million. Tremfya has increasingly replaced lost Stelara revenue following recent approvals in inflammatory bowel diseases. Sales of blood cancer treatment Darzalex rose about 16% to $4.24 billion, short of analyst expectations of $4.4 billion. J&J shares closed at $263.73 on Monday. They have risen 27% this year, outperforming both the broader market and most healthcare peers. The company posted third-quarter revenue of $25.4 billion, above analysts' average estimate of $25.28 billion, and adjusted earnings of $2.59 per share also topped Wall Street expectations of $2.54.
